rows.text: Under Article 25(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, the categories listed in Annex I, Part A always require a notified body, through module G, module H, or module B followed by module C. These are the removable transmission devices, vehicle servicing lifts, cartridge-operated fixing machinery, self-evolving safety components, and ML-based safety systems.

value: module B followed by module C
rows.text: For machinery in categories listed in Annex I, Part A, the manufacturer shall apply one of the procedures in Article 25(2): module B followed by module C, module H (full quality assurance), or module G (unit verification).

rows.value: Safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour fall under Annex I, Part A, point 5 of the Regulation.
rows.text: Such a safety component falls under the category of safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour in Annex I, Part A, point 5 of the Regulation.

rows.value: Interlocking movable guards must be used instead of fixed guards where frequent access is envisaged (Regulation, Annex III, point 1.3.8.1).
rows.text: Under Regulation Annex III, point 1.3.8.1, guards for moving transmission parts must be interlocking movable guards rather than fixed guards where frequent access is envisaged.

value: risks of contact which could lead to accidents
psychological stress that may be caused by the interaction with the machinery
rows.text: Under essential requirement 1.3.7 of Annex III of the Regulation, the risks addressed are contact risks that could lead to accidents (where risks persist), contact risks leading to hazardous situations, risks related to moving parts, psychological stress from interaction with the machinery, and accidental blockage of moving parts.

rows.value: The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification is treated as the manufacturer under Art. 18 of the Regulation, and must ensure and declare conformity on its sole responsibility; a non-professional user modifying machinery solely for its own use is not considered a manufacturer.
rows.text: Under Article 18 of the Regulation, the natural or legal person carrying out a substantial modification (one that affects the safety of only the machinery or a related product in an assembly) becomes subject to the manufacturer's obligations and must ensure and declare conformity on its sole responsibility; a non-professional user modifying machinery for its own use is excluded.

Under the Machinery Regulation, Article 10(8) requires machinery to be accompanied by the EU declaration of conformity, and Article 13(4) requires importers to ensure it is also accompanied by the instructions for use and the information referred to in Article 10(7).

technical documentation and EU declaration of conformity must be kept for at least 10 years (P10Y), on the condition: after the machinery or the related product has been placed on the market or put into service (source: REG, Art. 10(3)).
Regulation applies from 2027-01-20, on the condition: However, the following Articles shall apply from the following dates (source: CORR, Corrigendum, point 10).

rows.value: INAIL carries out the first periodic verification of Annex VII equipment, within 45 days of receiving the complete request.
rows.text: Under DM 2011 art. 2, c. 1, INAIL carries out the first periodic verification, which must be completed within 45 days of receipt of the complete request; INAIL may delegate it to an authorised body named by the employer.
The employer must keep the results of the checks for at least the last three years (P3Y), as set by art. 71, c. 9 of D.Lgs. 81/2008.

All 14 two-post lift models in the MAHA declaration of conformity (mastar-manual, section 10) are vehicle servicing lifts. Under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Annex I, Part A, point 3, and Article 25(2), they need a notified body from 20 January 2027 (Article 54). Units placed on the market under Directive 2006/42/EC before that date remain saleable under Article 52(1).

The facts do not say which category RC-5 falls under, so the required conformity assessment procedure from 20 January 2027 cannot be determined from them; the Regulation applies from that date (Corrigendum point 10), but the procedure depends on RC-5's category under Article 6 and Article 25.
The facts do not say whether model CS-400 may stay with internal production control after 20 January 2027, so no answer can be given.

rows.text: The Regulation's Annex III, section 1.1.9 ('Protection against corruption') introduces this essential requirement, which has no counterpart in the Directive's essential health and safety requirements.

rows.value: The ASL, or ARPA where regional law provides, or qualified public or private bodies, chosen freely by the employer.
rows.text: Under D.Lgs. 81/2008, art. 71, comma 11, later periodic verifications are carried out at the employer's free choice by the ASL, or by ARPA where regional law provides, or by qualified public or private bodies. DM 2011, art. 2, comma 1 names the ASL as holders of these later verifications, but the higher-ranking statute prevails.

The first periodic verification must be carried out within 45 days of the request, under Article 71, paragraph 11 of Legislative Decree 81/2008. The facts do not support the sixty-day figure attributed to the 11 April 2011 Ministerial Decree for the first verification; that decree's stated limit (30 days) applies to subsequent verifications.
